title: United States — Freedom of Information Act (1966)
t: United States — Freedom of Information Act (1966)
description: 5 U.S.C. § 552: the federal law giving the public the right to request records from federal agencies, with a 20-business-day statutory response clock and nine exemptions.

title: United Kingdom — Freedom of Information Act (2000)
t: United Kingdom — Freedom of Information Act (2000)
description: The UK's FOI Act, fully in force on 1 January 2005, covering over 100,000 public authorities with a 20-working-day response deadline.

title: Sweden — Freedom of the Press Act (1766)
t: Sweden — Freedom of the Press Act (1766)
description: The world's oldest freedom-of-information law: Sweden's 1766 Tryckfrihetsförordningen and the offentlighetsprincipen, the principle of public access.

title: India — Right to Information Act (2005)
description: India's RTI Act, in force 12 October 2005, giving citizens a 30-day right to information from public authorities for a 10-rupee fee.

title: Mexico — General Transparency Law (2015)
description: Mexico's transparency framework: the 2002 federal law, the 2015 Ley General de Transparencia, and the INAI guarantor body.

title: South Africa — Promotion of Access to Information Act (2000)
t: South Africa — Promotion of Access to Information Act (2000)
description: PAIA: South Africa's access law, unusual worldwide for covering private bodies as well as public ones.

title: Brazil — Access to Information Law (2011)
description: Law 12.527/2011, in force 16 May 2012: Brazil's access regime with a 20-day deadline and active-transparency duties.

title: Landmark disclosure — The Pentagon Papers (1971)
description: Daniel Ellsberg's 1971 leak and New York Times Co. v. United States (403 U.S. 713): the prior-restraint precedent behind modern disclosure law.
